title: DIY Hardwood Floor Refinishing vs Hiring a Pro in Edmonds: The Real Cost Comparison
meta: DIY refinishing saves money on paper but costs two weekends and a risk of sanding mistakes. Wills Flooring compares DIY vs pro costs for an Edmonds floor.
keywords: DIY hardwood floor refinishing cost, refinish hardwood floors yourself vs professional, drum sander rental hardwood floors, hardwood floor refinishing Edmonds WA, is DIY floor refinishing worth it

blocks.lead: On a typical 700 sq ft Edmonds main floor, doing it yourself costs roughly a third of the professional price in rentals and materials, but it also costs two to three full weekends, and one sanding mistake erases the savings because the fix is a full professional sand anyway.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring's published rate is $3.99 per sq ft for a natural finish, labor and Bona finish included, 500 sq ft minimum. The DIY figures below are typical rental and retail numbers, not Wills prices.

blocks.html: A common Reddit thread goes like this: an Edmonds couple pulls the carpet in a Seaview rambler, finds oak, rents a drum sander for the weekend, and then posts photos asking why the floor has waves in it. DIY refinishing can work, and we have seen good results from patient homeowners in Westgate and Perrinville. But the comparison people run in their heads leaves out the rental hours, the second trip for abrasives, the finish you cannot buy at retail, and the chance of a mistake only a pro can fix. This post puts real numbers on both columns.

blocks.text: Where DIY jobs go wrong, and what the fix costs

items.title: Drum sander stop marks
items.text: A drum sander cuts the moment it touches the floor. Pause for a second and it digs a dish you can see in raking light forever. The fix is a full professional re-sand, so you pay the pro price on top of the rentals.

items.title: Edger swirls and a halo
items.text: The edger sands across the grain in circles. Without a final pass with a random orbital, every wall shows a lighter band with swirl marks once the finish goes on.

items.title: Sanding through thin wood
items.text: Older Edmonds floors have been sanded before. Fir in the Bowl can be down to a few sixteenths above the tongue. A rental drum takes off more than you expect, and once you hit the tongue the board is done.

items.title: Finish problems
items.text: Lap lines, bubbles from shaking the can, dust nibs from sanding and coating in the same room, and a coat that stays tacky because it went on thick. Each one means abrading and recoating the whole room.

blocks.text: When DIY is the right call

a.title: The odds are on your side
items: The floor is a small, square room with few walls and closets
You want a natural finish, not stain
The wood is thick and has never been sanded
You have done it before, or have a patient friend who has
The house is empty and your time is cheap right now

b.title: The mistake would be expensive
items: The floor is fir, or oak that has been sanded before
You want stain or a light Scandinavian tone
There are stairs, a long hall or many closets
You are selling and buyers will look in raking light
You need it done in days, not weekends

blocks.title: One Edmonds-specific warning:
blocks.text: Homes near downtown and in the Bowl are often 1920s to 1940s with old-growth fir. Fir is soft, shows every sander wobble, and has usually been sanded before. We measure the remaining thickness before we quote, and sometimes a recoat is all the floor can safely take. A rental drum does not know that. If you have fir, read our post on refinishing old fir floors first.
If you hire: what to ask. If you DIY: what to do first.

items.html: Ask whether a recoat is enough. If the finish is dull but nowhere worn to bare wood, a $1.99 screen and recoat beats both columns above.
Measure the wood before you sand. Pull a heat register and look at the board edge. Less than an eighth of an inch above the tongue means no more full sandings, DIY or pro.

Understand dust. Rental drums throw dust everywhere. Our sanders are vacuum-connected and the $250 containment option seals doorways and runs an air scrubber. See how dustless refinishing really works.
Get the finish named on the quote. Wills Flooring uses three coats of Bona water-based finish and we are Bona Certified Craftsmen, which is why the finish carries a real warranty.

Get the free estimate anyway. We measure, check the wood and hand you a firm written price on the spot. It is the cheapest way to test your DIY number, and it costs nothing if you still do it yourself.

faq.q: How much does it cost to refinish hardwood floors yourself?
faq.a: For a 700 sq ft floor, sander and edger rentals for two to three days plus abrasives, retail finish and supplies come to roughly a third of the professional price, before counting 30 to 40 hours of your time. Those are typical rental and retail figures, not Wills Flooring prices.

faq.q: How much does a professional refinish cost in Edmonds?
faq.a: Wills Flooring's published price is $3.99 per sq ft for a natural finish and $6.50 with stain, both all-in with labor and three coats of Bona finish, 500 sq ft minimum. A 700 sq ft Edmonds main floor is $2,793 natural, or $3,043 with dust containment.

faq.q: Can a beginner use a drum sander on hardwood floors?
faq.a: Yes, but it is unforgiving. A drum cuts the moment it touches the floor, so any pause leaves a dish. Beginners do better with a rental orbital sander, which is slower but much harder to damage a floor with. Practice in a closet first.

faq.q: What is the most common DIY refinishing mistake?
faq.a: Sanding a floor that only needed a recoat. Second is edger swirls along every wall. Third is sanding through a thin floor, which is common on older Edmonds fir. All three are why we measure the wood and check the finish before quoting.

faq.q: Is DIY refinishing worth it to save money before selling?
faq.a: Usually not. Buyers in Edmonds walk floors in daylight and stop marks, swirls and lap lines show. A professional natural refinish at $3.99 per sq ft is one of the highest-return pre-sale jobs, and a visibly amateur one can cost more in the negotiation than it saved.

faq.q: Can I refinish just one room myself and have a pro do the rest?
faq.a: You can, but matching sheen and color between a retail finish and a Bona finish is difficult and the seam shows at the doorway. If a pro is coming for most of the house, the extra room at $3.99 per sq ft is rarely worth the mismatch.
